question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 10-trading-day (Sep 21-Oct 2 = exactly 10 sessions) return differences between front-month WTI futures and S&P 500 futures; long-run median is roughly -0.5 (oil drift ~0, equities ~+0.5%/2wk), and that is my anchor. The 2026 Hormuz-crisis regime widens dispersion enormously without clearly shifting the center: overlapping 10-day WTI windows this quarter ran -7% (early Aug, reopening hopes), +1% (mid-Aug), +22% (Sep 1-15), +14% (Sep 4-18). Center pulled slightly negative by three things: an ~$25-30 geopolitical premium versus analyst Q4-26 Brent targets of $70-90 (JPM $80, EIA ~$90) and a spike catalyst that is visibly being mitigated by Saudi rerouting; negative near-term momentum (3 down sessions, -0.5% on the week); and a probable front-month roll inside the window (CLV26 expires ~Sep 22, curve backwardated in a supply crisis) worth roughly -1% to -2% if the resolver uses unadjusted continuous prices. Offsetting: live war with repeated reignitions, winter demand, record diesel, and an equity leg facing a hiking Fed with the 10y near 5% (a falling S&P widens the spread upward). Those roughly cancel, so I sit just below the base rate with very wide, mildly left-skewed tails. Open bounds are priced: a war-ending deal could collapse the premium (early Aug showed -7% on mere reopening expectation; March-to-August was ~-35%) past -25, and a Hormuz closure or a direct hit on export infrastructure could clear +25 (Feb-Apr ran +58%). Evidence here is decent on prices/levels and thin on forward catalysts inside the window, which argues for staying close to the anchor rather than leaning on any narrative.

calls.reference_class: Biweekly (10-trading-day) windows, 2015-2026, of front-month WTI crude futures percentage price return minus S&P 500 futures percentage price return

calls.reasoning: Class median is about -0.5pp (equities carry drift, front-month crude does not). Three adjustments move the center below every member run. (1) The crude leg's roll falls inside the window - CLV26 expires ~Sep 22 with Oct/Nov backwardated ~4.6% - and 'Crude Oil Futures' is vendor-series naming, where continuous front-month crude is unadjusted and books that step; at ~62% weight on unadjusted, net of ~+1% roll-yield accrual on the Nov leg over the 8 post-roll sessions, that is ~-1.7pp. The S&P leg rolled at the Sep 17-18 triple witching, so it carries no offsetting step. (2) A modest negative news tilt: Saudi throughput recovered to 2.8 mb/d, Ras Tanura ship-to-ship sales, China pressing Iran on Houthi strikes, WTI rejecting $106 and closing $100.30 on three straight down sessions. (3) Against that, a hiking Fed (Sep 16 +25bp, >50% odds in October), a ~5% 10-year and the Oct 2 jobs report make the equity leg's expected return roughly flat, which offsets part of the drag. Direction is close to a coin flip; dispersion is the content, and with a live Hormuz war both bounds have named mechanisms - a settlement unwinding a $25-30/bbl premium below -25, a Hormuz closure or Abqaiq-scale strike above +25.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes were: (a) the September OVX level - 47.17 @ Aug 18 (Runs 1/3, no Sep print) vs 61.13 mid-Sep (Run 2); unsettleable without retrieval, so I took OVX ~55 between them and sized dispersion off that rather than picking a side. (b) The roll convention - the criteria text was empty for all three runs, so nobody could confirm it; I weight unadjusted front-month at ~62% because the question's instrument names are vendor-series names and vendor continuous crude is unadjusted, and Run 2's sourced Oct/Nov quote ($101.3 vs $96.6) sizes the step at ~4.6%, which I net down to ~3% for post-roll roll-yield accrual. This is why my median (-2.8) sits below all three runs (-1.0, -1.5, -2.0): they each haircut the same artifact harder than the evidence supports, and Run 3 did not size it at all. (c) Dispersion 18/23/26 - pure judgment, broken by recomputing from implied vols rather than averaging: 24. (d) Escape mass - set at 4.5%/3.5%, the asymmetry following mechanically from the shifted median, not from a directional view. Settled and uncontested: the equity leg rolled before the window (no ES roll artifact), no OPEC+ meeting confirmed inside Sep 21-Oct 2, and no prediction market matches this contract (Kalshi's WTI markets are price-level only - wrong instrument, wrong window), so no crowd anchor was applied.
